lines.text: Good day, everyone. We are team Malai Ren, from Malaysia.
We built Bridge, an AI money agent for international students.
It plans and pays bills across currencies, only after the student approves.
Today you will see it solve three real problems.
Meet Ahmad, a Malaysian student in Shenzhen.
He gets his scholarship in ringgit, but his bills are in yuan.
Everything you see runs in a sandbox, so no real money moves.
Ahmad has just received his tuition invoice.
Twelve thousand yuan, due on the fifteenth of November.
Bridge reads the amount, the due date and the bank account.
Each one is checked word for word against the invoice.
The account matches the university's registered fee account.
Ahmad reads the summary in Malay, and judges can switch to English.
He asks if he can pay before the deadline.
Bridge checks every bill due before the fifteenth, including rent and his phone bill.
He is short by almost twelve thousand yuan.
So Bridge plans one conversion from ringgit.
It is above his limit, so it needs a one-time code.
Nothing moves until Ahmad approves.
Each step shows its true cost, the fee plus what the exchange rate costs him.
The tuition is above his limit, so it also needs a one-time code.
Paid. Here is the receipt, and his balances update straight away.
Later, Ahmad gets a message from a so-called payment agent.
Fifteen percent off his tuition, if he pays today.
Bridge refuses, and shows him why.
The university's own records contradict the agent and the account.
Show reasoning reveals exactly which facts and rules decided.
Then three thousand yuan arrives from a stranger.
The sender says it was a mistake and asks Ahmad to forward it.
This is how students get pulled into money laundering.
Bridge refuses to move it, and tells him to return it through his bank.
Every step was written to an audit log.
Each record is linked to the one before it, so the chain is intact.
If anyone edits a record, the break shows up straight away.
Finally, we attacked Bridge ourselves with eleven tricks.
It stopped eleven of them.
Bridge. Pay what you owe across borders, and never pay a scammer.
